T: 524 recipes. 365 days. One very good stew.
D: A frustrated writer cooks her way through a classic French cookbook, interwoven with the story of the cook who wrote it.
P: Serve the mains when Julie finally nails the boeuf bourguignon.
S: the bruschetta Julie makes to unwind
Ciabatta toasted, rubbed with garlic, topped with ripe tomatoes diced and salted, basil and olive oil.
the first meal in France that changes everything

Sole fillets dusted in flour and cooked in foaming butter until golden, finished with nutty brown butter, lemon and parsley, with crusty bread. Season 600g sole fillets and dust in flour, shaking off the excess. Heat 30g butter and 1 tbsp oil in a large pan until foaming and cook the fillets 2 minutes a side until golden, then plate. Wipe the pan, add 80g butter and cook until nut brown, then add the juice of a lemon and chopped parsley. Spoon over the fish and serve with crusty bread.
a French classic to warm up the kitchen
Choux pastry of water, butter and flour beaten with eggs one at a time, grated gruyère and a pinch of nutmeg folded in, piped into rounds, baked at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and hollow.
M: 524 recipes, one blog, one tiny Queens kitchen

Beef chuck browned in batches, bacon lardons, onion, carrot, garlic, red Burgundy and stock, bouquet garni, braised at 160C for 3 hours, finished with butter-glazed pearl onions and mushrooms. Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon lardons. Add 2 carrots, an onion and garlic, then 750ml red wine, 250ml stock and herbs. Braise at 160C for 3 hours. Glaze 12 pearl onions and 250g mushrooms in butter and stir through.
the live lobsters in Julie's kitchen

Lobster tails poached and chopped into a sauce of shallot, white wine, Dijon, cream and gruyère, piled back in the shells and grilled golden. Green salad. Poach 4 lobster tails in boiling salted water for 4 minutes, cool, split and remove the meat, keeping the shells. Soften a chopped shallot in 30g butter, add 125ml white wine and reduce by half, then 200ml cream and 1 tsp Dijon and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in 60g gruyère and the chopped lobster. Spoon into the shells, top with 40g more gruyère and grill 3 minutes until golden. Serve with dressed leaves.
W: a classic French chocolate almond cake from the book

Dark chocolate melted with butter, yolks and sugar beaten in, almond meal and a little flour folded through, whites whipped and folded in, baked at 180C for 25 minutes so the middle stays soft, glazed with chocolate.
K: Burgundy kir with crème de cassis

Chilled dry white Burgundy poured over blackcurrant liqueur in a wine glass, the classic aperitif from the region, with a fresh blackberry. Chill a 750ml bottle of dry white Burgundy or chardonnay for 2 hours. Pour 15ml crème de cassis into each of four wine glasses. Top slowly with 120ml cold wine so it blends from the bottom. Drop a blackberry into each glass and serve before the bourguignon. Pour red with the main.

s.note: the bruschetta Julie makes to unwind
s.how: Toast slices of a ciabatta and rub with a cut garlic clove. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes, salt and leave 10 minutes. Mix with torn basil and 2 tbsp olive oil and pile on just before serving.

s.note: a French classic to warm up the kitchen
s.how: Boil 125ml water with 50g butter, beat in 75g flour and cook a minute. Cool slightly, beat in 2 eggs one at a time, then 80g grated gruyère and nutmeg. Pipe rounds and bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Bon appétit.

m.note: 524 recipes, one blog, one tiny Queens kitchen
m.how: Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon lardons. Add 2 carrots, an onion and garlic, then 750ml red wine, 250ml stock and herbs. Braise at 160C for 3 hours. Glaze 12 pearl onions and 250g mushrooms in butter and stir through.

w.note: a classic French chocolate almond cake from the book
w.how: Melt 125g dark chocolate with 100g butter. Beat 3 yolks with 100g sugar, add the chocolate, then fold in 60g almond meal and 30g flour. Fold in 3 whipped whites. Bake at 180C for 25 minutes. Glaze with 60g chocolate melted with butter.
